service_name: VA Internal Medicine — General Medicine Wards (VAMC)

source.source_file: CWRU IM Residency — VAMC General Medicine Wards Learning Objectives

prior_to_rotation: Review VAMC general medicine wards learning objectives (intern level applies to psychiatry off-service rotators)
Confirm call schedule with team — interns on 4-day rotating call (long-medium-short-happy)
Review procedure credentialing requirements on IM procedure website if expecting procedures
overview: Psychiatry PGY off-service rotation on VAMC general medicine wards (CWRU IM program service). Case-based teaching with bedside attending rounds; two residents + one attending per team. Psychiatry rotators typically carry intern-level primary responsibility: admissions H&P overnight, daily exams, progress notes, discharge summaries, and day-to-day management under senior resident and attending supervision.
location: Wade Park VA — general medical inpatient wards
Patients from VAMC ED, transfers from surgical/neurology floors, direct admissions, ICU/other hospital referrals
personnel: Ward team: two IM residents + one teaching attending
Intern (or psych rotator in intern role): primary responsibility for assigned patients
Senior resident: supervises two interns, co-admissions, daily rounds on all service patients
Attending: ultimate responsibility; staffs new admissions within 24h; cosigns notes
schedule: Regularly scheduled attending rounds — majority bedside teaching
Chief Rounds, M&M Conference, morning report augment attending teaching
logistics: Intern objectives: acute H&P, collateral, labs/imaging interpretation, differential, targeted exams tracking pathophysiology, emergent stabilization, therapeutic planning, resource utilization, psychosocial/contextual factors, humanistic care, care coordination and safe transitions (ambulatory, SNF, rehab, subacute)

Resident objectives: advanced evaluation, prioritized differentials, teach juniors physical exam, manage emergencies and guide juniors, resource utilization, interdisciplinary communication, transitions of care
Admission H&P on chart night of admission; attending staffs following morning
Daily progress notes; examine every assigned patient every day; discharge summaries on all patients

Procedures (when credentialed/supervised): thoracentesis, arthrocentesis, LP, NG tube, IV, phlebotomy, ABG, paracentesis — resident must supervise if credentialed; attending supervises key portion unless urgent
Mid-rotation feedback strongly encouraged; end-of-rotation written eval; anonymous resident→attending eval
Teaching method: case-based discussions + recent literature applied to service cases
resources: Recent medical literature applied to cases on service
IM procedure credentialing website (supervised procedure counts)
debrief_prompts: Admission you owned overnight — differential, workup, and what changed after attending staffed
Procedure or bedside exam finding that clarified pathophysiology
Discharge planning — handoff to ambulatory, SNF, rehab, or subacute; what systems barriers appeared?
Resource utilization or psychosocial factor that shaped the plan
Teaching moment — when a senior or attending pushed your clinical reasoning
